title: Gpu Versatility
definition: The ability of GPUs, which are primarily designed for graphics processing, to be utilized for other computational tasks such as running language models.

difficulty_levels.beginner: GPUs are like multi-taskers in a computer. They're great at playing videos smoothly and making video games look good, but they can also help with tasks like running language models, which can make your computer work faster.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: GPUs are not only used for graphics processing. They excel at matrix multiplication, a type of mathematical operation that's essential for running language models. This is why tools like Llama.cpp can utilize the GPU for language model processing, improving speed and reducing CPU load.
difficulty_levels.expert: The versatility of GPUs is a fascinating aspect of computer architecture. While GPUs were initially developed for graphics processing, their ability to perform matrix multiplications has led to their adoption in various computational fields. This parallel processing capability makes GPUs exceptionally efficient for running language models. However, the distinction between 'GPUs for graphics' and 'GPUs for AI' is more about software utilization than hardware design. The same GPU can perform both functions, with the distinction being what software is running on it. This duality highlights the overlap between different fields in computer science.

extra_fields.insight: GPUs are not just for graphics; they can be utilized for running language models, offering improved speed and reduced CPU load.
